subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu direct session can become unusable after /reset or /new and fall back to generic 'Something went wrong...' while session index points to missing transcript IDs

question: For direct-chat `/reset` and `/new`, should OpenClaw require a durable transcript before publishing the new session mapping, or allow publication with an explicit repair/remap fallback?
rationale: Both shapes can address missing transcript lineage, but they differ in user-visible reset semantics, failure recovery, and whether missing empty reset sessions are treated as invalid state.

options.title: Transactional rotation
options.body: Create or prewarm the new transcript before updating the session store or lineage, keeping the previous transcript authoritative if creation fails.

options.title: Repair-after-publication
options.body: Allow the mapping to advance, but immediately detect missing transcript files and remap to the newest valid family member with specific recovery copy.

options.title: Fold into broader UX work
options.body: Leave this narrow durability issue open only as linked context under the broader Feishu failure-status policy issue.

recommendation.title: Transactional rotation
recommendation.body: Create or prewarm the new transcript before updating the session store or lineage, keeping the previous transcript authoritative if creation fails.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner on the inspected reply initialization and session accessor lines.
